The OPP’s Project ARDEN files fit a larger Canadian pattern: police leadership treated political dissent as a security problem while treating inconvenient facts as something to ignore.   Officers who questioned modelling, Pfizer data, or reported adverse events among colleagues and the public were monitored. The same command structure that had “no threat” findings still kept the surveillance going because those officers might give legitimacy to people opposing government overreach.   That is not neutral law enforcement. It is political policing.  This did not happen in isolation.   During COVID, forces across the country were directed to enforce public-health orders with a zeal they rarely apply to chronic violent crime, auto theft rings, or rural property crime.   The Freedom Convoy then showed the inverse: bank-account freezes, coordinated intelligence requests on people who were not committing crimes, and political pressure for background checks that even an OPP intelligence chief flagged as ethically offside.   RCMP and municipal services have a long record of similar mission creep—G20 joint intelligence, historical surveillance of Indigenous political organizations, and more recent use of tools that blur public-health tracking with political monitoring.   When the institution’s priority is protecting the “status quo” rather than investigating whether the status quo is lawful or evidence-based, corruption of purpose follows.  Add the ordinary kind of corruption on top of the political kind.   Ontario is now running a province-wide inspection after Toronto officers were charged with selling data to organized crime.   That is not a one-service problem.   Weak vetting, sloppy database access, and a culture that protects the organization first show up in force after force.   Oversight bodies that still rely on police investigating police, or that can only recommend rather than compel, do not break that cycle.  Correction requires structural change, not another press conference.  Operational independence has to be real.   Ministers and premiers set the law; they should not set who gets watched for holding the wrong opinion on a vaccine or a mandate.   Intelligence collection on lawful speech and association by serving or retired officers should require a criminal threshold, not a “discomfort to the status quo” test.  Oversight must be fully civilian, independently funded, and armed with subpoena power, binding timelines, the ability to initiate systemic reviews, and a clear path to criminal referral.   Police-investigating-police for serious misconduct should end.   Leadership appointments—commissioners, chiefs, deputy ministers of public safety—need transparent criteria that reward fidelity to the Criminal Code and evidence, not political reliability.  Whistleblower protection for officers who raise data, safety, or legality concerns has to be statutory and meaningful.   The people Gircys describes were treated as the threat instead of as sources. That inversion is how institutions go blind.  Database access, promotion, and internal discipline need independent audit.   Body-worn cameras and public reporting of use-of-force and political-direction incidents should be default, not optional.   Where the record already shows coordinated suppression of dissent or refusal to examine harms, a public inquiry with full document production is the minimum.  Police exist to keep the peace and enforce the law equally.   When they become an enforcement arm for a government’s narrative, they stop being a police service and start being a political instrument.   Canada has the statutes and the oversight architecture on paper.   It has not used them to restore that distinction.   That is the work that still has to be done.  free-speech.ca

Democrats want unreasonable locks on United States AI   Bernie Sanders takes the harder line. He treats advanced AI as an existential risk that should not be left to “Big Tech oligarchs.”  He and Rep. Greg Casar introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (Sept. 2026). It would permanently ban development or deployment of ASI (AI that exceeds human cognitive performance across most domains or could destroy or disempower humanity) and immediately pause other advanced AI work until a new federal agency writes and enforces safety rules. He has written to the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta telling them to pause development and “stop building machines that humans cannot control.” With Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez he sponsored a federal moratorium on new AI data centers until “strong national safeguards” exist. He argues the U.S. should also push for international agreements, including with China, because a runaway superintelligence would be a global problem, not just an American one.  Elizabeth Warren also wants to slow frontier work, but she has not gone as far as a permanent ASI ban.  She has called for an immediate pause on advanced AI development while Congress and regulators put safety systems in place. She wants legislation that creates stronger guardrails before an AI-facilitated cyberattack, economic crisis, or national-security disaster occurs. She has broken with Sanders by stopping short of endorsing a ban on superintelligence. Reporting has also noted she favors taxing AI companies as part of the policy mix.  In short: Sanders wants a pause plus a hard ban on superintelligence and a new federal agency; Warren wants a pause on advanced systems and statutory guardrails, without the same explicit ban.

That is fewer than the previous week, but the severity, concentration and amount of compromised data moved in the opposite direction.  1️⃣ FEWER ATTACKS, HIGHER IMPACT  The weekly count fell from 445 to 396, roughly 11%, yet attacks classified as critical increased from 52 to 58.  Hackmanac’s average ESIX severity score also rose from 4.46 to 4.62.  Even more striking, claimed compromised data jumped from 30.1 TB to approximately 133.2 TB.  The relevant signal is therefore not declining cyber activity. It is increasing damage per meaningful incident.  2️⃣ THE WEEK’S MOST IMPACTED TARGETS SHOW HOW BROAD THE RISK HAS BECOME  Hackmanac places DataHub Nepal, Gyazo and MPA Pharma at an ESIX of 7.96, followed by Astemo at 7.45 and Gc789 Network / Boundless Te at 7.42.  There is an important journalistic distinction here: DataHub and Gyazo have independently documented incidents, while some ransomware listings involving MPA Pharma and Astemo remain threat-actor claims that have not received equivalent victim-side confirmation.  Cyber intelligence is useful only when “claimed” and “confirmed” remain separate categories.  3️⃣ GOVERNMENT INFRASTRUCTURE REMAINS THE PRIMARY BATTLEGROUND  Government, military and law-enforcement organisations accounted for 82 incidents, or 20.7% of the week’s total.  NoName057(16) was the most active actor tracked by Hackmanac, claiming responsibility for 34 attacks, while the United States remained the most affected country with 81 incidents.  This reflects a structural change in cybersecurity: disruption is increasingly used alongside conventional political, military and economic pressure.  4️⃣ DATAHUB NEPAL — WHEN A CYBERATTACK CLOSES A STOCK MARKET  One of the week’s most economically significant incidents occurred in Nepal.  A ransomware attack against DataHub Pvt. Ltd., which hosted systems used by 72 brokerage firms, disrupted TMS trading infrastructure, CDSC-related services and payment connections.  The Nepal Stock Exchange subsequently suspended trading.  This is the point where cybersecurity becomes financial stability.  The attacker did not need to manipulate prices or steal securities. Disabling a concentrated infrastructure provider was enough to interrupt access to an entire capital market.  5️⃣ GYAZO — THE VALUE OF METADATA IS OFTEN UNDERESTIMATED  Helpfeel confirmed that attackers gained unauthorized access to Gyazo and exposed approximately 23.62 million user records.  The breach also involved metadata associated with roughly 490 million images.  The exposed fields included email addresses, password hashes, session IDs, integration tokens, upload IPs, EXIF location information and OCR-extracted text. Payment-card numbers were not exposed.  For financial organisations, the lesson is broader than Gyazo itself: screenshots, collaboration tools and informal SaaS applications can contain trading screens, internal dashboards, wallet addresses, client information and authentication material.  “Metadata” can be financially sensitive data.  6️⃣ HARUKO — INSTITUTIONAL CRYPTO HAS A SUPPLY-CHAIN PROBLEM  Haruko provides portfolio, risk and trading infrastructure connecting institutional crypto firms with exchanges and blockchain venues.  The attack affected 15 clients and reportedly exposed read-only exchange API information and trading data. Some smaller clients were also reported to have suffered financial losses.  The affected clients were non-whitelisted.  This matters because institutional crypto increasingly depends on middleware: portfolio systems, custodians, API gateways, analytics platforms and execution infrastructure.  An institution can secure its own wallet architecture and still inherit the vulnerabilities of a provider sitting between it and the market.  7️⃣ DCENT — SELF-CUSTODY DOES NOT END AT “I OWN THE KEYS”  DCENT confirmed unauthorized asset transfers involving its App Wallet and warned that potentially exposed wallets include those whose recovery phrase had previously been entered into the software wallet and had signing history on affected versions.  The company explicitly distinguished this from a confirmed compromise originating inside its hardware wallets.  Independent XRPL analysis subsequently traced six attack waves between September 15 and 20 involving approximately 11.75 million XRP across thousands of wallets.  The important lesson is architectural.  A hardware device can remain uncompromised while a recovery phrase previously exposed to software destroys the security boundary that hardware was supposed to provide.  8️⃣ NOSTRA — AN ORACLE PRICE IS NOT LIQUIDITY  Nostra’s Starknet money market suffered an approximately $3.5M incident after manipulation of the thin NSTR market allowed inflated collateral to support borrowing of ETH, STRK, USDC, USDT, WBTC and DAI.  Pragma’s own post-incident analysis is particularly important: NSTR was already considered a high-risk feed because of limited liquidity and pricing sources.  This exposes a recurring DeFi mistake.  Knowing the last traded price of an asset does not mean millions of dollars of that asset can actually be liquidated at that price.  Price discovery without market depth is not robust collateral valuation.  9️⃣ FOMOPEEK AND FLAMINCOME — OLD AND NEW ATTACK SURFACES COEXIST  FomoPeek demonstrates the modern endpoint problem: a malicious crypto-tracking application distributed through Apple’s App Store was linked to nearly $580K in stolen USDT and reportedly contained methods capable of breaking normal iOS isolation.  At the opposite end of the stack, legacy Flamincome contracts lost roughly $346K after an attacker used an approximately $18M flash loan to manipulate vault share accounting.  One incident targeted the device.  The other targeted old DeFi logic.  Both produced financial loss.  🔟 THE REAL FINANCIAL SIGNAL  Cybersecurity is no longer an isolated IT function.  A modern financial position depends on a chain of infrastructure:  exchange → API → custodian → wallet → device → oracle → cloud provider → data centre → communications provider → human operator.  Each additional dependency increases operational efficiency, but also creates another potential point of failure.  This week demonstrated that cyber losses do not need to begin with stolen money.  They can begin with unavailable brokers, manipulated collateral, compromised metadata, leaked API information, poisoned software or a weak third-party provider.  From an investor’s perspective, cybersecurity should therefore be treated alongside liquidity, counterparty exposure and operational resilience.  It is becoming a component of capital preservation itself.  📲 t.me/m4x3_crypto_channel 📚 amazon.it/dp/B0GX311NWG?bind…  DYOR — NFA  #CyberSecurity #Finance #Crypto #Bitcoin #DeFi #Web3Security #Ransomware #DigitalAssets #SelfCustody #CyberRisk

An open port doesn’t necessarily mean the service you expect is actually there.  A SYN/ACK confirms that something answered the connection. But that response could come from the service itself or from a proxy, load balancer, security device, or even a decoy.  ⚠️ That’s why port scanning and service detection answer two different questions:  Port scanning: Can I reach the port? Service detection: What is actually responding?  The distinction matters. Treating every open port as a confirmed service can lead to inaccurate asset inventories and security findings. 🚨 Threat Actor Claims Breach of Bupa Australia Exposing 4.23M Customer Records  A darkweb forum post alleges that a threat actor has obtained a massive dataset containing personal and financial information of 4.23 million customers of Bupa Australia. The post, published on an underground forum, claims the data was extracted in CSV format and is being offered for sale at a price of $400.  According to the listing, the compromised dataset includes highly sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and insurance-specific details for each record. The exposed fields reportedly include: - Membership numbers - Full names, dates of birth, and sex - Mobile phone numbers and email addresses - Full street addresses, suburbs, states, and postcodes - Insurance cover types, hospital tiers, and extras levels - Premium amounts, rebates, and payment frequencies - Claims history from the last 12 months and benefits paid  Bupa Australia is one of the two largest private health insurers in the country and operates as a subsidiary of the British group Bupa Group. The company serves millions of Australians with health insurance products. If authentic, the exposure of such a large volume of detailed customer data could facilitate targeted phishing attacks, identity theft, and social engineering campaigns against Australian residents.  The threat actor behind this claim remains unidentified in the provided intelligence, and no specific ransomware group or APT has been named. At the time of reporting, Bupa Australia has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the alleged data leak has not been independently verified by security researchers.

🚨 Darkweb Post Claims Leak of Classified US Intelligence on PLA Cyber Modernization  An anonymous post on an underground forum alleges the theft and sale of highly classified documents originating from U.S. intelligence sources. The actor claims the leaked materials detail the People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) strategic shift toward informationized and intelligentized warfare, with a specific focus on cyber operations, electronic warfare, and artificial intelligence integration.  According to the listing, the documents outline PLA procurement and capability-development efforts in several advanced domains: *   Portable drone jammers and integrated counter-drone systems *   AI-enabled deepfake content generation and large-model AI platforms *   Real-time broadcast interception and drone leasing programs *   Expansion of cyber-reconnaissance infrastructure using overseas cloud nodes and residential proxy networks  The post further asserts that the intelligence reveals the PLA Strategic Support Force's transition into dedicated Information Support, Aerospace, and Cyberspace Forces, indicating a drive to formalize these domains for future conflict and strategic competition. The actor claims the files include assessments of complex contingencies, such as the US–Israel–Iran confrontation.  The threat actor invites potential buyers to a private session for verification and samples, explicitly warning that scammers will not be entertained. The source of the thread does not identify the specific threat group responsible for the alleged breach, nor does it provide independent proof of authenticity beyond the description of the content. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by U.S. authorities or major security firms.

🚨 Chevron Faces Alleged Data Breach and September 25 Ransom Deadline  A threat actor operating under the handle ShadowByt3S has posted a ransom demand against Chevron Corporation on an underground forum, alleging unauthorized access to multiple internal systems including Okta and Nigeria-based infrastructure. The post, dated September 23, 2026, claims the group has exfiltrated sensitive data and is currently holding access to compromised portals, threatening further escalation if a ransom is not paid by September 25, 2026, at 5:00 PM New York time.  According to the listing, the alleged breach exposes a wide range of sensitive information across different operational sectors of the energy giant. The claimed data includes:  *   **PII & Financial Data:** Live bank routing details, personal identifiers (names, employee IDs, home addresses), and comprehensive payroll records dated September 13, 2026, including specific earnings and tax withholdings. *   **Industrial Control Systems (ICS):** Technical logs for fire and gas systems in Nigeria, detailing unpatched Autronica fire alarm panels and ICS network configurations connected to enterprise management architectures. *   **Supply Chain & Procurement:** Purchase orders, equipment serial numbers, and vendor catalogs for critical infrastructure such as the Escravos LPG FSO vessel, along with internal contact lists for procurement engineers. *   **Retail Operations:** A directory of physical gas station and car wash locations, including store coordinates and facility classification codes. *   **Commercial Transactions:** B2B transaction ledgers from Latin America, specifically Colombia, tracking invoices in Colombian Pesos for lubricant products like Delo 400 XLE.  The actor alleges they have breached specific endpoints, including okta.chevron.com, tqnigeria.chevron.com, cbp.lubricants.chevron.com, and saseoi.azure.chevron.com. The post claims that passwords for two of these portals have been changed by the attackers to prevent immediate recovery, asserting that they are "still inside" the network. Screenshots purportedly showing access to Okta and other internal tools were attached to the forum post as proof of compromise.  Chevron Corporation is one of the largest publicly traded energy companies in the world, with operations spanning exploration, production, refining, and chemical manufacturing across numerous countries. A breach involving ICS logs and supply chain data could pose significant operational risks if authentic, potentially exposing vulnerabilities in safety-critical infrastructure. At the time of reporting, Chevron has not publicly commented on the incident, and the breach has not been independently verified.

⚠️ Threat Actor Claims 22M Russian Borrower Records Leaked from Dozarplati  A post on the darkweb forum ShinLeaks alleges that a database containing 22 million verified borrower records from Dozarplati, a major Russian digital micro-credit and payday loan provider, has been compromised. The threat actor claims the dataset includes sensitive financial data derived from the platform’s AI-driven underwriting engine, which processes instant approvals for loans up to 100,000 rubles.  According to the listing, the exposed data is not merely a list of contacts but a comprehensive financial footprint of users who have passed stringent Know Your Customer (KYC) verification required by the Central Bank of Russia. The actor describes the dataset as containing: *   Regulatory and KYC verification data for all profiles. *   Active banking details and routing information linked to user accounts. *   Behavioral credit data and device footprints used for credit scoring. *   Financial histories indicating active cash flow and short-term liquidity usage.  Dozarplati operates as a significant player in the Russian FinTech sector, offering micro-loans through a mobile application and operating under licensed corporate entities such as MKK Soyuz 5. The platform is known for its high-volume, short-term lending model and cross-sells insurance products to its user base. The actor asserts that because the platform’s algorithms are optimized to minimize non-performing loans, the leaked records represent a "high-quality" pool of vetted consumers with proven digital financial activity.  The post invites potential buyers to review the data schema via direct message and initiate an escrow transaction. At the time of reporting, Dozarplati has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the authenticity of the claimed 22 million record dump has not been independently verified.

sample_tweets.text: 🧰 10 GITHUB REPOSITORIES WORTH BOOKMARKING FOR CYBERSECURITY RESEARCH  A strong security toolkit is not just about scanners and exploits.  Sometimes the most useful resource is a well-maintained repository with payload references, wordlists, public reports, OSINT resources, training labs, and field-tested notes.  Here are 10 worth keeping close:  * swisskyrepo/PayloadsAllTheThings — payload encyclopedia and attack references * danielmiessler/SecLists — huge collection of wordlists and test data * HackTricks-wiki/hacktricks — practical pentesting and privilege-escalation field guide * jivoi/awesome-osint — curated OSINT tools and resources * edoardottt/awesome-hacker-search-engines — search engines useful for security research * reddelexc/hackerone-reports — collection of public HackerOne reports * edoardottt/awesome-hacking — broad hacking and security resource list * Orange-Cyberdefense/arsenal — security tools and research inventory * OWASP/Top10 — OWASP Top 10 project resources * OWASP/WebGoat — deliberately insecure application for hands-on security training  Why these matter:  * Better payload and testing references * Faster reconnaissance and enumeration * Stronger OSINT workflows * Real-world vulnerability writeups * Practical labs for continuous learning * Easier access to trusted community knowledge  Analyst Note:  The best repository is not always the one with the most stars.  What matters is whether it is maintained, relevant, and useful to your workflow.  Bookmark the good ones. Revisit them often. And always validate techniques in a legal, controlled environment.  #DDW #CyberSecurity #GitHub #OSINT #Pentesting #RedTeam #SecurityResearch #OWASP #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 COMPROMISED GITHUB ACTIONS CAME BACK ONLINE — MINI SHAI-HULUD TAGS STILL LIVE  Socket researchers report that two popular actions-cool GitHub Actions — issues-helper and maintain-one-comment — were re-enabled on September 16, 2026 with malicious release tags still intact from the May Mini Shai-Hulud campaign.  • Both repos were originally compromised May 18 and disabled by GitHub security on May 19 • On re-enablement, mutable tags such as @v2.2.1 still resolved to the malicious payload • Any workflow referencing either action by tag (not a pinned commit SHA) resumed downloading and running the malware • Payload installs Bun, harvests CI/CD secrets from the runner, and exfiltrates them • GitHub’s dependency graph lists ~15,000 repositories depending on issues-helper alone • Socket update Sep 25: both repositories have been disabled on GitHub again — tag-based workflows now fail at job setup instead of executing the payload  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is Socket primary research (published Sep 24, updated Sep 25), not a dark-web claim. The material new fact is the Sep 16 re-enablement with unclean tags, plus today’s second disable. Treat prior May compromise details as background. Workflows pinned to a known-clean pre–May 18 commit SHA were not hit by the tag move. 🚨 $351.6M BITGET HACK — NORTH KOREAN ACTORS SUSPECTED  Bitget has confirmed that approximately $351.6 million was stolen after attackers compromised a critical backend system supporting its wallet infrastructure.   According to Bitget, the attackers were able to spoof transaction data and trigger the platform’s authorization process, resulting in unauthorized transfers from a portion of its hot and warm wallets. The company says its cold wallets were not affected.   Bitget has temporarily suspended withdrawals while the incident is investigated. Deposits and trading remain operational, and the company says customer balances are accurate and the losses are covered by its User Protection Fund.   Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said the attack pattern is highly consistent with known North Korean threat actor activity based on IP behavior and on-chain analysis. However, attribution to the Lazarus Group specifically has not yet been publicly confirmed.   ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The important detail here is the attack path. Bitget says the attackers did not need to steal private keys; instead, they compromised backend wallet infrastructure and manipulated transaction data before the authorization-signing process. Fraudsters impersonated Intesa Sanpaolo CEO Carlo Messina through a fake WhatsApp message sent to then-chairman Paolo Molesini, then reinforced the scam with a phone call using an AI-cloned voice impersonating lawyer Paolo Nastasi of A&O Shearman and spoofed emails containing payment instructions.  About €40 million was recovered in China and another €13 million was frozen in Portugal, but at least €36 million remains missing, with some of the funds reportedly converted into cryptocurrency. 🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-09-26 09:26 KST

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 공격자들은 AI 에이전트를 활용해 공격 실패 시 재시도 비용을 낮추고, 자동화된 공격 파이프라인을 구축하여 대규모 침해를 시도하는 경향이 뚜렷합니다 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/the-soc-doesnt-need-to-start-over-with.html)). 특히, 정상적인 소프트웨어 도구(Tailscale, GitHub Actions 등)를 악용하여 탐지를 회피하거나, ClickFix와 같은 사회공학적 기법으로 사용자의 직접적인 실행을 유도하는 방식이 고도화되고 있습니다 ([Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/threat-intel/2026/09/kothamine-malware-uses-tailscales-tailcat-to-evade-network-detection)). 또한, 공개된 취약점(CVE)이 발표된 직후 수 시간 내에 대규모 스캔 및 익스플로잇이 발생하는 'Zero-day' 대응 속도전이 가속화되고 있습니다 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208601)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **ShinyHunters (UNC6240):** [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-hacked-clop-leak-site-using-grav-cms-path-traversal-flaw/) 및 [DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyber-risk/what-we-missed-google-gemini-ai-escape-party) 근거. Clop 랜섬웨어 그룹의 데이터 유출 사이트를 해킹하고, Oracle PeopleSoft 취약점을 대규모로 악용하여 웹쉘을 배포함.
- **Larva-25012:** [AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95515/) 근거. 2026년 하반기 Proxyware를 활발히 유포하며 감염된 시스템을 프록시 네트워크의 일부로 악용.
- **Storm-3168 (JADEPUFFER):** [DFIR_Radar](https://twitter.com/DFIR_Radar/status/2103545962849587308) 근거. Azure 서비스 주체를 탈취하여 7분 만에 스토리지 및 키 볼트를 파괴하는 자동화된 공격 수행.

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **Metaencryptor 랜섬웨어:** 한국 카메라 모듈 및 장비 제조 기업을 대상으로 공격 수행 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95544/)).
- **Beast(GodDamn) 랜섬웨어:** 국내 의료기관을 대상으로 RDP 취약점을 악용하여 침투 및 보안 제품 무력화 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5779)).
- **개인정보 불법 유통:** 올해 1월~7월 사이 한국인 관련 개인정보 불법 유통 게시물 8만 9천여 건 탐지 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208603)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-93399:** WordPress Bookly plugin, CVSS 9.1, Unauthenticated IDOR, PoC 공개 ([ridvanyagli](https://twitter.com/ridvanyagli/status/2103635847408968151)).
- **CVE-2026-86350 / CVE-2026-41293:** Apache Tomcat, CVSS 9.1, HTTP/2 Request Smuggling, PoC 공개 ([ridvanyagli](https://twitter.com/ridvanyagli/status/2103625079124828486)).
- **CVE-2026-71336:** Windows Work Folder Service, CVSS 8.8, Integer overflow, RCE 가능 ([DFIR_Lab](https://twitter.com/DFIR_Lab/status/2103636991615078505)).
- **CVE-2026-87902:** WordPress Core, CVSS 미상(High), Unauthenticated path traversal, KEV 등재 및 실제 악용 중 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208601)).
- **CVE-2025-39682 / CVE-2026-53266 / CVE-2025-39964:** Linux Kernel, CVSS 미상(High), KEV 등재 및 실제 악용 중 ([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/product-tech)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE:** CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2026-53266, CVE-2025-39964 ([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/product-tech)), CVE-2026-87902 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208601)), CVE-2026-42608 ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-hacked-clop-leak-site-using-grav-cms-path-traversal-flaw/)).
- **도메인:** third-party[.]com (ClickFix 캠페인 악용) ([Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/09/criminals-turn-placeholder-domain-into-clickfix-trap)).

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **WordPress 패치:** CVE-2026-87902에 대해 즉시 최신 버전으로 업데이트하고, 관리자 계정 생성 여부를 로그에서 확인하십시오.
